title: Map reads
intro: Pick the assay and where your reads come from; the page writes the commands that take them to mapped output with nf-core, through the lab's lab-rnaseq, lab-atacseq, lab-chipseq and lab-proseq commands, and stops there. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

script.name: Shechter Lab map-reads command builder
script.waits:
map --status --watch,
# status after fetch and map

inputs.label: FASTQ folder
inputs.hint: Raw reads already on the cluster.

inputs.label: Public data
inputs.hint: GEO, SRA or ENA accessions, downloaded with nf-core/fetchngs.

fields.label: I have not installed the pipelines yet
ChIP-seq flavour (assay_type)
fields.hint: Written to assay_type in the project config; CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag map with nf-core/cutandrun.

fields.label: Experiment folder
fields.hint: One folder per dataset; the nf-core output goes inside it.

fields.label: Project folder
fields.hint: init creates it (a relative path is made absolute).

fields.label: FASTQ folder
fields.hint: Absolute path to the folder holding the .fastq.gz files.

fields.label: FASTQ file names
fields.hint: Paste the output of ls on that folder, one name per line. R1/R2 mates are paired for you (_R1/_R2, _1/_2, .R1/.R2); a file without a mate is single-end. Lanes such as _L001 become extra rows of the same sample.

fields.label: Single-end reads (every file is its own read 1; CTRL_1, CTRL_2 are replicates, not mates)
Strandedness
fields.hint: PRO-seq libraries are almost always stranded: check your kit's documentation.

fields.label: Accessions
fields.hint: GEO (GSE, GSM), SRA (SRR, SRX, SRS, SRP, PRJNA, SAMN), ENA (ERR, ERX, PRJEB, SAMEA) or DDBJ ids, separated by lines, spaces or commas.

fields.label: nf-core profile (fetchngs)
fields.hint: The container runtime of your cluster; the lab's usual one is singularity.

fields.label: Genome
fields.hint: A refgenie genome name; the references must be staged (see the install step).

sections.title: Advanced (optional)
sections.summary: Extra nf-core parameters, revision, output folder, run and project names, a dry run only. Empty fields change nothing.

fields.label: Extra nf-core/rnaseq parameters (YAML file)
fields.hint: For example 3' mRNA-seq or UMI settings.

fields.label: nf-core/rnaseq revision
fields.hint: Empty uses the launcher's pinned version.

fields.label: nf-core output folder
fields.hint: Empty writes nfcore_rnaseq/ in the experiment folder, where lab-rnaseq setup looks for it.

fields.label: Map run name
fields.hint: Names the run under results/map/; empty uses map_<timestamp>.

fields.label: Project name
fields.hint: init --name; empty uses the folder's name.

fields.label: Dry run only: write the job scripts, submit nothing

session.comment: Every session: activate the lab environment

blocks.title: write the nf-core samplesheet from the FASTQs

lines.comment: Check the sample names in samplesheet.csv are <group>_REP<n> (edit the sample column if not): lab-rnaseq setup drafts metadata and contrasts from them.

blocks.title: download the public reads with nf-core/fetchngs

lines.comment: lab-rnaseq has no fetch command: run nf-core/fetchngs directly. Paste your accessions in the '3. Your reads' section and this step writes accessions.csv (one id per line, no header).
Nextflow is in the lab_nextflow env (setup.sh builds it): conda activate lab_nextflow first, then conda activate lab_pipelines again. This runs on this node and can take hours: use tmux or screen.
Once fetchngs has finished. --nf_core_pipeline rnaseq makes it write a samplesheet nf-core/rnaseq accepts (strandedness auto).
fetchngs names the samples after the experiment accessions: edit the sample column to <group>_REP<n> (lab-rnaseq setup drafts metadata and contrasts from them).
Wait for the mapping job to finish.
Dry run only: nothing was submitted. Untick the dry run to get the submit and status lines.
The mapped output is nfcore_rnaseq/ (or your output folder). The analysis starts from it with lab-rnaseq setup: see the RNA-seq analysis page.
init writes inputs/project_config.yaml; if your cluster needs a Slurm account, set project.slurm_account there.
The genome comes from --genome below; references.organism / reference_alias in the config is used later by the analysis, so set it to match.

blocks.title: write the samplesheet from your FASTQ names

lines.comment: Paste your FASTQ file names in the '3. Your reads' section (for example the output of ls on the FASTQ folder): this step then writes inputs/samplesheet.csv for you.
Paste your accessions in the '3. Your reads' section: this step then writes inputs/accessions.csv (one id per line, no header: the file nf-core/fetchngs reads).
fetch submits a Slurm job. Repeat the status line until it has finished.
Dry run only: the job script is written, nothing is downloaded or submitted. Untick the dry run to get the steps that follow.
fetchngs names the samples after the experiment accessions and sets every replicate to 1: edit the sample and replicate columns of inputs/samplesheet.csv.

The fetched samplesheet is at results/fetch/fetch/output/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv. Write inputs/samplesheet.csv from its sample, fastq_1 and fastq_2 columns, with the header sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,replicate,antibody,control: replicate numbers, each sample's antibody, and as control the sample name of its Input/IgG (blank for the Input/IgG samples).

The fetched samplesheet is at results/fetch/fetch/output/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv. Write inputs/samplesheet.csv from its sample, fastq_1 and fastq_2 columns, with the header sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness and forward or reverse (not auto) as strandedness.
For public data: once the fetch has finished and inputs/samplesheet.csv is edited.
map submits a Slurm job. Repeat the status line until it has finished.
Dry run only: the job script is written under results/map/, nothing is submitted. Untick the dry run to get the submit and status lines.
The mapped output is results/map/<run name>/output/ in the project folder (nf-core's own layout). The analysis (analyze, compare, report) is not part of this page.
